newsitem.title: INDIA: India takes extra Saudi crude, no hurry for Iraq oil.
newsitem.headline: India takes extra Saudi crude, no hurry for Iraq oil.

text.p: Indian Oil Corp (IOC) expects to import more crude from Saudi Arabia this year than originally contracted for but is not in the running for an immediate purchase from Iraq under the United Nations' oil-for-food scheme, IOC chairman R.K. Narang said on Thursday.
IOC expected to purchase seven million tonnes (140,000 barrels a day) of Saudi crude instead of the 120,000 bpd contracted for, he said.
But he would not comment on IOC purchases of Saudi crude next year.
He said IOC was in contact with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) but that no concrete oil purchase was under consideration.
"We will be looking into the arrangements for Iraqi supplies under the U.N. agreement but at the moment all I can say is that we are in touch.
Iraq is hoping in the near future to start crude sales under the long-delayed oil-for-aid agreement signed with the United Nations last May.
India was one of Iraq's biggest customers before the United Nations enforced an embargo after Baghdad sent troops into Kuwait in August 1990.
